title: TEXICO HOME FIRE
full_story:
A Home in rural Texico was damaged by an early Saturday morning fire.

The Kell Fire Department received a report just after 2 am that the Ronald Shurtz home was on fire.  Shurtz woke up when his CPAP machine quit working and found smoke throughout the home.

Firefighters arriving on scene found smoke showing from the front door and attic.  Fire was found in and around the HVAC unit and had extended into the attic.  The fire was brought under control a short time later.  The homeowner was treated at the scene and later went to the hospital with a family member for further examination.

Firefighters were on scene for just over 2 hours.  The Salem Fire Protection District provided mutual aid at the scene, while Iuka, Centralia Fire Protection District, and Mt. Vernon firemen staged once it appeared there would be a quick knockdown.

title: CRIME SUPPRESSION DETAIL
full_story:
Illinois State Police (ISP) conducted a violent crime suppression detail on May 13th and 14th, in St. Clair and Madison counties, focusing its efforts on East St. Louis and neighboring Metro East communities.  The operation utilized intelligence and technology to focus enforcement efforts on known high crime areas, violent offenders, and structured criminal groups in the communities of the Metro East.

Troopers made 23 arrests, filed 33 total criminal charges, made 25 felony arrests and filed 15 firearm related charges.  There were 11 firearms seized, 3 of which had been reported stolen, 818 grams of cannabis and 93 grams of other controlled substances were seized.  Also 2 stolen vehicles were recovered.

ISP officers from around the state, including Troops 6, 7, 8, and 10 patrol, ISP Fatal 4 South, Zone 6 Firearms Investigations Unit, Public Safety Enforcement Group (PSEG), Crime Scene Services, ISP SWAT, ISP Air Operations, and the FBI, assisted ISP Statewide Anti-Violence Enforcement (SAVE) South with this multi-day operation.

title: 5th ANNUAL MASONIC AUCTION
full_story:
The 5th Annual Flora Masonic Lodge Auction will take place Saturday, May 30th at 10:00 am at the Clay County Fairgrounds in Charley Brown Park.

Anyone can donate, to make a donation call 618-843-3815.  Checks and money orders should be made out to the Shriners Hospital and mailed to Don Fry at 323 East 4th Street in Flora.  Donations will be accepted within a 50-mile radius of Flora.  The auction flyer also contains a QR Code that can be scanned to make a donation directly to the Shriner’s Hospital.  The auction never fails to offer many useful and intriguing items.  Dagg’s Auction Service will be the auctioneer.

All Proceeds from this auction will help support the life changing specialized pediatric healthcare provided by the Shriners Hospital for Children.  Last year the auction raised $14,293 for the Children’s Hospital.

title: CDL REIMBURSEMENT PROGRAM
full_story:
In an effort to address the growing need for CDL truck drivers in the Illinois Basin oil production industry, the Illinois Petroleum Resource Board (IPRB) will be offering a CDL training/certification cost reimbursement program to oil production companies that are contributing to the IPRB assessment.

IPRB will reimburse qualifying companies for expenses up to $2,500 per employee seeking a CDL license.  Eligible expenses include training or schooling fees, required medical exams, DMV testing fees, and truck rental or access fees.  Companies will be required to submit proof of CDL license obtained, current employment at the company and receipts for any training or schooling, medical test fee and DMV test fee to qualify for reimbursement.

Text or call IPRB executive director Seth Whitehead at 618-367-4751 if you are a qualifying company that is interested.

title: S.U.R.E. SYMPOSIUM
full_story:
The Clay County Health Department is collaborating with the Coalition Against Drug Abuse of Clay County, the Clay County Board, SIU School of Medicine, and Birth to Five Illinois to bring the second Substance Use Resource & Education Symposium or S.U.R.E Symposium to Clay County on August 11th.  Registration will begin at 8:30 am at the Oil Belt Christian Service Camp.

The goal of the S.U.R.E. Symposium is to bring together local agencies, experts, and community members to provide a safe space to learn about substance abuse prevention, recovery, and what happens after.

Lunch will be provided to the first 200 who register, and continuing education units are pending.  Register by going to tinyurl.com/SURE2026 or use the QR code on the health department’s website.  This years symposium registration is being covered by the Clay County Board Opioid Settlement.

title: OUTLAND AIRPORT SELECTED
full_story:
Mt. Vernon Outland Airport has been selected as the Terminus host site for the 2026 Air Race Classic, marking a major milestone for both the airport and Mt. Vernon.  The nationally recognized event will bring pilots, crews, aviation officials, and visitors from across the country to Mt. Vernon, making it the largest aviation event hosted at the airport since the 1973 Blue Angels air show.

The Air Race Classic is a prestigious, all-female piloted cross-country air race that traces its roots to the 1929 Women’s Air Derby.  The modern race challenges teams to fly a multi-day route across the United States, testing accuracy, flight planning, and consistency rather than pure speed.  The race concludes at the designated Terminus city, where pilots are welcomed and celebrated for their achievement.  More information about the race is available at airraceclassic.org.

“Being selected as the Terminus for the Air Race Classic is a tremendous honor for Mt. Vernon Outland Airport,” said Chris Collins, Airport Manager.  “This event puts our airport on a national stage and highlights the professionalism of our facilities and staff.  It’s exciting to host an event of this scale and significance.”

Racers and race officials are expected to begin arriving on Thursday, June 25th, and will remain in Mt. Vernon through Monday, June 29th, participating in a variety of planned events, receptions, educational opportunities, and community activities throughout their stay.

“This is truly a community-wide opportunity,” said Sheila Jolly Scrivner, Host City Terminus Chair.  “From aviation enthusiasts to families and local businesses, the Air Race Classic offers something for everyone, and we’re looking forward to showcasing Mt. Vernon’s hospitality and support for women in aviation.”

A public aviation celebration and youth activity day will be held on Saturday, June 27th, from 9 am to 3 pm at Mt. Vernon Outland Airport.  Activities will include Young Eagle Flights for children, interactive aviation displays, educational opportunities, and additional family-friendly programming designed to inspire the next generation of pilots and aviation professionals.

Event organizers are actively seeking local, regional, and national sponsors to support the 2026 Air Race Classic Terminus and related activities.  Sponsorship opportunities will offer businesses and organizations high-visibility exposure, community engagement, and alignment with a nationally respected aviation event that promotes education, skill, and opportunity for women pilots.

The Air Race Classic is a nonprofit organization dedicated to encouraging and educating women pilots, increasing public awareness of general aviation, and honoring the legacy of women in aviation through an annual cross-country air race.

More than 12 million Illinois residents are connected to access to housing, food, healthcare, and other essential needs through 211 services.

Every Illinois resident can now dial 211 to connect to services that offer help getting basic needs such as housing, food, health care, and mental health services.  211 Illinois announced the completion of statewide coverage.

“Statewide 211 coverage is a major milestone for 211 Illinois,” said David Wortman, board chair.

The nonprofit said the three-digit number works as a free, confidential, 24/7 starting point for people who aren’t sure where to turn.  Call specialists can help residents find local programs, check what services they may qualify for, and provide referrals.  The help includes rent or utilities assistance, finding food pantries and nutrition programs, locating clinics, and connecting to counseling, crisis, and caregiver support.

The statewide directory includes more than 35,000 verified resources.

“Statewide 211 coverage is a major milestone for 211 Illinois,” said David Wortman, board chair.

Residents can reach the service by calling 211, texting a ZIP code to 898211, or visiting https://211illinois.org and selecting “Search for Help.”
